rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i reads abrogation here more broadly than legislative repeal: the verses’ purposes can be qualified, with worship the universal end and mercy the realized end for those guided.
rows.anchor: وفيها دلالة على أخذه عليه السلام النسخ في الآية أعم من النسخ الواقع في التشريع

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report in al-Nu'mani attributes to the Imam the reading of 21:101–102 as abrogating the universal statement that all will come to Hell in 19:71: the people promised good are kept away.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير النعماني أيضا عنه عليه السلام قال ونسخ قوله تعالى { وإن منكم إلا واردها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects treating 19:71 and 21:101–102 as a general verse qualified by a particular one: an irrevocable divine decree cannot be lifted or invalidated.
rows.anchor: أقول وليست الآيتان من قبيل العام والخاص لقوله تعالى { كان على ربك حتما مقضيا }

rows.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir is reported to include badaʾ among forms of abrogation, citing God's erasing and confirming what He wills, and the deliverance of Jonah's people.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن الباقر عليه السلام إن من النسخ البداء المشتمل عليه قوله تعالى { يمحوا الله ما يشاء

rows.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
rows.claim: Some reports from the Imams count the death of one Imam and the succession of another as abrogation; al-Tabataba'i says he explained this earlier and that reports on such meanings are abundant.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار عن أئمة أهل البيت عد عليه السلام موت إمام وقيام إمام آخر مقامه من النسخ

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports that God lifted verses and caused the Prophet to forget them; he glosses the replacement as bringing something lighter, a concession, a command, or a prohibition.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال كانت الآية تنسخ الآية وكان نبي الله يقرأ الآية والسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects the reports that explain the verse as God making the Prophet forget recited material because they contradict the Qur'an, as discussed under “or cause it to be forgotten.”
rows.anchor: وجميعها مطروحة بمخالفة الكتاب كما مر في بيان قوله أو ننسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim restricted his request to believers after sensing its universal reach, while recognizing that ordinary social life makes provision of fruits depend on nonbelievers too; God's answer therefore included both.
rows.anchor: ولذلك لما استشعر ما استشعره من عموم دعوته قيدها بقوله من آمن منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to Ibrahim's prayer operated through customary conditions and natural law, without a break in ordinary causation.
rows.anchor: وفيه بيان أن المستجاب من دعوته ما يجري على حكم العادة وقانون الطبيعة من غير خرق للعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains that Ibrahim asked for fruits for the town as a distinction honoring the sacred House; a barren valley could not produce fruit or sustain residents otherwise.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل وارزق من آمن من أهلة من الثمرات لأن المطلوب استيهاب الكرامة للبلد لكرامة البيت المحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets' prayers are governed by spiritual realities and nearness to God, not outward self-interest; Ibrahim had no favoritism toward descendants, as his disavowal of his father shows.
rows.anchor: ولو كان له هوى لبدأ فيه لأبيه قبل ذريته ولم يتبرأ منه لما تبين أنه عدو لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As evidence against personal ambition, al-Tabataba'i notes that Ibrahim did not ask to escape shame at resurrection or for a celebrated reputation; he asked only for remembrance among later generations.
rows.anchor: بل اكتفى بلسان ذكر في الآخرين إلى غير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Islam Ibrahim requested for his descendants is genuine submission to God; the phrase “for You” signals its reality, since a merely nominal Muslim community would not need that qualification.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى { أمة مسلمة لك } ، إشارة إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i identifies the requested messenger as Muhammad; the Prophet said, “I am Abraham's prayer.”
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى { ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم } الخ، دعوة للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Kattani asked al-Sadiq about someone who forgot the two rakʿahs at Abraham's station during pilgrimage tawaf: if still in Mecca, pray there; if already departed, do not return.
rows.anchor: في الكافي عن الكتاني قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن رجل نسي أن يصلي الركعتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the ruling details—praying at or behind the station, including the report that tawaf's two rakʿahs must be behind it—are inferred from the preposition “from” and the word “prayer place.”
rows.anchor: مستفادة من لفظة من، ومصلى من قوله تعالى { واتخذوا من مقام إبراهيم مصلى

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq explains God's order to purify the House for pilgrims as removing the polytheists from it.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي عن الصادق عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { أن طهرا بيتي للطائفين

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says a servant should enter Mecca in a state of purity, after washing away sweat and dirt, citing the command to purify the House.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي عن الصادق عليه السلام قال إن الله عز وجل يقول في كتابه { طهرا بيتى للطائفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the purity expected of visitors from the purity of the place may also be inferred from verses such as “the good women are for good men.”
rows.anchor: واستفادة طهارة الوارد من طهارة المورد، ربما تمت من آيات أخر، كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that Abraham tested Ishmael's two wives: he told Ishmael to replace the inhospitable first, blessed the hospitable second, left his footprints on the station stone while she washed his head, and signaled that the household threshold was sound.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع عن ابن عباس قال لما أتى إبراهيم بإسماعيل وهاجر

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Qummi transmits al-Sadiq's account: after Sarah's distress, God directed Abraham to take Hajar and Ishmael to Mecca; Hajar searched for water, Zamzam appeared, Jurhum settled there, and Abraham and Ishmael later built the House and performed pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي، عن الصادق عليه السلام قال إن إبراهيم كان نازلا، في بادية الشام

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Within the same report, God compares a woman to a crooked rib: leaving it brings enjoyment, while trying to straighten it breaks it; this precedes the order to take Hajar and Ishmael away.
rows.anchor: إن تركتها استمتعت بها، وإن أقمتها كسرتها

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq glosses the fruits as people's hearts: God made others love Ibrahim's family so people would feel at ease with them and keep returning.
rows.anchor: من ثمرات القلوب، أي حببهم إلى الناس، ليستأنسوا بهم، ويعودوا إليهم

rows.speaker: بعض الأخبار
rows.claim: Some reports say the House first existed as a luminous dome sent down to Adam, remained at the site until Noah's flood, then was raised while the site stayed above the flood, earning the name al-ʿAtiq.
rows.anchor: فلما غرقت الدنيا رفعه الله تعالى، ولم تغرق البقعة، فسمى لذلك البيت العتيق

rows.speaker: بعض الأخبار
rows.claim: Other reports say the House's foundations descended from Paradise and the Black Stone descended whiter than snow, then darkened when touched by unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وفي بعضها ان الحجر الأسود نزل من الجنة - وكان أشد بياضا من الثلج - فاسودت لما مسته أيدي الكفار

rows.speaker: أحدهما عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Kafi reports that God ordered Abraham to build the Kaaba, raise its foundations, and teach people the rites; as he and Ishmael reached the Black Stone, Abu Qubays returned the trust stone to Abraham.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي أيضا عن أحدهما عليه السلام قال إن الله أمر إبراهيم ببناء الكعبة، وان يرفع قواعدها

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir is reported to say three stones came from Paradise: the Black Stone entrusted to Abraham, Abraham's station, and the stone of the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن الثوري عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام، قال سألته عن الحجر، فقال نزلت ثلاثة أحجار من الجنة

rows.speaker: بعض الأخبار
rows.claim: Some reports identify the Black Stone as an angel.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار أن الحجر الأسود كان ملكا من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says these reports are numerous in Sunni and Shiʿi traditions; although individually solitary rather than mutawatir, their volume and parallels give no reason to reject them wholesale.
rows.anchor: وهي وإن كانت آحادا غير بالغة حد التواتر لفظا، أو معنى، لكنها ليست بعادمة النظير في أبواب المعارف الدينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dome's descent and Abraham's travel by Buraq are extraordinary but not impossible; the Qur'an itself affirms many miracles and extraordinary favors granted to prophets.
rows.anchor: فهي أمور لا دليل على استحالتها، مضافا إلى أن الله سبحانه خص أنبياءه بكثير من هذه الآيات المعجزة، والكرامات الخارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He interprets reports of heavenly or hellish origins through a broader pattern: good things or vessels for good descend from Paradise and return there, while evil descends from Hell and returns to it.
rows.anchor: فما كانت منها خيرا جميلا، أو وسيلة خير، أو وعاء لخير، فهو من الجنة، وإليها تعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From 15:21 he derives that all things exist with God without limits, then become bounded and measured as they descend gradually into the world; he also cites livestock, iron, and provision from heaven.
rows.anchor: أفاد ان كل شيء موجود عنده تعالى وجودا غير محدود بحد، ولا مقدر بقدر، وعند التنزيل - وهو التدريج في النزول - يتقدر بقدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an also teaches that everything returns to God, as shown by verses stating that the end, return, and final destination belong to Him.
rows.anchor: وقد أفاد في كلامه ان الكل راجع إليه سبحانه، فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Between origination and return, things follow what their beginning calls for and the share of felicity or misery assigned to them, as expressed by verses on each person's way and direction.
rows.anchor: وأفاد أن الأشياء - وهي بين بدئها وعودها - تجري على ما يستدعيه بدئها، ويحكم به حظها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that natural things come from Paradise or Hell can therefore be sound in broad principle when tied to felicity or misery, though this does not establish the authenticity of every individual report.
rows.anchor: لا تخلو عن وجه صحة، لمطابقتها لأصول قرآنية ثابتة في الجملة، وإن لم يستلزم ذلك كون كل واحد صحيحا

words: وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَٰهِۧمُ ٱلْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلْبَيْتِ
rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: A hypothetical critic argues that the verse plainly means Abraham and Ishmael built the House in an idolatrous land, while storytellers added accounts of the House's antiquity, Adam's pilgrimage, and heavenly origins to embellish religion.
rows.anchor: وربما قال القائل إن قوله تعالى { وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت وإسماعيل } الآية، ظاهر في أنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects judging sacred honor by material origin: the House is honored as God's House and a site of worship, while the Black Stone is honored by its ritual status, not its substance or color.
rows.anchor: فشرف هذا البيت بتسمية الله تعالى إياه بيته وجعله موضعا لضروب من عبادته لا تكون في غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets' distinction likewise comes from God's choosing them for prophethood, not their bodies or clothing; worldly people could surpass them in wealth and adornment.
rows.anchor: وكذلك شرف الأنبياء على غيرهم من البشر ليس لمزية في أجسامهم، ولا في ملابسهم

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: A critic calls the traditions contradictory, poorly authenticated, and contrary to the Qur'an, and alleges that Jewish heretics spread Israelite fables to make Muslims' religion repellent to the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: قال وهذه الروايات فاسدة في تناقضها وتعارضها في نفسها وفاسدة في عدم صحة أسانيدها وفاسدة في مخالفتها لظاهر الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i concedes the critic has a point in part but says he overargues: contradictions matter only if every report must be accepted individually, not when the reports are considered together without a rational or textual impossibility.
rows.anchor: إن التناقض أو التعارض إنما يضر لو أخذ بكل واحد واحد منها، وأما الأخذ بمجموعها من حيث المجموع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For reports traced to the Prophet or the purified Household, contradiction among individual narrations does not require rejecting all; statements by non-infallible commentators among Companions and Successors are assessed like other human reports.
rows.anchor: وإنما نعني بذلك الروايات الموصولة إلى مصادر العصمة، كالنبى صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والطاهرين من أهل بيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the Qur'an and definitive Prophetic tradition bind in the foundations of divine religious knowledge; material conflicting with them must be rejected, while reports neither disproven by reason nor forbidden by them lack grounds for either acceptance or rejection.
rows.anchor: وبالجملة لا موجب لطرح رواية، أو روايات، إلا إذا خالفت الكتاب أو السنة القطعية، أو لاحت منها لوائح الكذب والجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weak chains alone do not warrant rejecting reports unless they conflict with reason or sound revelation.
rows.anchor: وبه يظهر فساد اشكاله بعدم صحة أسانيدها، فإن ذلك لا يوجب الطرح ما لم يخالف العقل أو النقل الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that Abraham built the visible house of stone and clay; it does not rule out a heavenly origin for the Black Stone or an earlier dome later raised from the site.
rows.anchor: وهل الآية تدل على أزيد من أن هذا البيت المبني من الحجر والطين بناء إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He attributes the critic's rejection of these reports to sectarian bias against metaphysical truths about prophets or unthinking reliance on modern natural science's material explanations.
rows.anchor: لعصبية مذهبية توجب نفي معنويات الحقائق عن الأنبياء، واتكاء الظواهر الدينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural science studies material properties, composition, and natural causal relations; social science studies social relations. Neither has jurisdiction to affirm or deny immaterial realities outside those fields.
rows.anchor: العلوم الطبيعية شأنها البحث عن خواص المادة وتراكيبها وارتباط الآثار الطبيعية بموضوعاتها، ذاك الارتباط الطبيعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Science can describe the stone and clay needed to build a house and social history behind Abraham's construction, but cannot decide whether a stone came from the promised Garden or Hell.
rows.anchor: وأما أنه ما نسبة هذا الحجرمثلا إلى الجنة أو النار الموعودتين فليس من وظيفة هذه العلوم أن تبحث عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an says natural material things descend from God and return to Him, and that deeds ascend to Him even though they consist of natural movements and socially conventional acts.
rows.anchor: وقد عرفت أن القرآن الشريف هو الناطق بكون هذه الموجودات الطبيعية المادية نازلة إلى مقرها ومستقرها من عند الله سبحانه
